charter.mission: We own the capital allocation of a conglomerate: which businesses get funded, which get sold, and which get told no. Our product is the portfolio, not any one thing in it.
charter.process: Division plans and the bets' quarterly gates come in once a year and a single group objective goes out. Divisions bring their numbers to a monthly business review; anything that trades one division's quarter against another's is settled there, in writing, and published to the group.
owns: the decision to start or shut a bet

charter.mission: We run the advertising-funded consumer business that pays for everything else in the group. Our job is to keep that engine growing while the products it funds slowly stop needing it.
charter.process: We plan one operating budget across Search, Ads, Streamside, Maps, Commerce, Platforms and Hardware, reviewed monthly against revenue per user rather than per product. Product decisions that move ad load or default placements come to us before they ship, because they move the group's funding.

charter.mission: We are the first place a person goes when they want to know something, and we intend to stay that even when the answer arrives without a link to click.
charter.process: Quality changes run through a live experiment and a human rater panel before launch; nothing ships on offline metrics alone. We hold a weekly quality review where the rater data and the complaint queue are read out before anyone shows a graph.
owns: generated answers on the results page

charter.mission: We turn attention into revenue for the group and into measurable customers for advertisers, and we try to do it with fewer ads each year rather than more.
charter.process: Advertiser demand and publisher supply are planned as one market. Auction and format changes go through a revenue-impact review with Finance and a user-impact review with Search or Streamside before launch, and we publish the take rate we charge.

charter.mission: We want Streamside to be where a creator can make a living, because a platform that only pays the top thousand people is one good competitor away from empty.
charter.process: Creator payouts, subscription revenue and ad revenue are planned together against one number: creators earning a full-time income. We review the payout formula quarterly with Creator Partnerships in the room and publish changes 90 days before they take effect.

charter.mission: We keep the map of the world accurate enough that people trust it for the last mile, and we want local businesses to transact on it rather than merely appear on it.
charter.process: Freshness comes from three streams: imagery, business-supplied edits and user reports, reconciled nightly. Licensing renewals are planned 18 months out because a country going dark is not a quarter we can recover.

charter.mission: We want the search for a product to end on our surfaces instead of starting on ours and finishing on a marketplace, which means owning the checkout and not only the click.
charter.process: Retailer inventory feeds, checkout and fraud are one system with one on-call. Merchant onboarding runs self-serve by default; anything requiring a human is treated as a bug in the onboarding flow and written up.

charter.mission: We keep the group's software on the devices people actually buy, from someone else's phone to a headset that does not exist yet, so the consumer products are never a guest on a rival's platform.
charter.process: One OS release train a year, monthly security drops, and a developer preview that opens six months ahead. Partner OEMs get the release on the same day we do; anything that would give first-party hardware an advantage goes to Legal before it ships.

charter.mission: We build the group's own devices, and this year we intend them to pay for themselves rather than serve as a demonstration of what the software could do on better silicon.
charter.process: Programs run on an 18-month clock from architecture lock to mass production, with a cost gate at nine months that kills the program rather than trimming it. Silicon and Devices plan as one roadmap because the margin lives in the gap between them.

charter.mission: We are the group's second engine. We are not trying to win on price; we are trying to stop being the vendor that gets added to the comparison slide and never to the shortlist.
charter.process: Enterprise commitments are forecast weekly from a single pipeline with Cloud Sales. Feature bets come from lost bake-offs rather than from competitor feature lists, and every loss is written up with the reason inside five days.

charter.mission: We do the frontier research and we get it into products people already use. A model that only exists in a paper has not done its job, and a product that ships a model we cannot explain has not done its either.
charter.process: Research runs on its own clock; productisation runs on the divisions'. Applied AI holds a shared serving stack that every first-party surface uses, so a model improvement reaches nine products at once. No frontier launch leaves the gate without Model Safety signing it off.

charter.mission: We are trying to prove that driverless transport is a business with unit economics, not a demonstration that gets renewed every year because it looks like the future.
charter.process: City launches run off a written playbook rather than a launch team, and a city that needs a team is a playbook bug. Safety data is collected continuously and published quarterly with the raw incident records, whether or not a regulator has asked.

charter.mission: We turn health research into products a clinician will actually order. Our failure mode is nine promising pilots and nothing a patient can be prescribed.
charter.process: Every program carries a named buyer and a regulatory path from day one, reviewed at the quarterly gate; a program that cannot name both is stopped rather than reduced. Trial results are published in full, including the arms that did not work.
owns: regulatory clearance for group health products

charter.mission: We connect people that terrestrial networks will not reach for another twenty years, at a cost per covered user a carrier in that market can actually pay.
charter.process: We do not sell to consumers. Coverage is sold wholesale to national carriers on multi-year contracts, and the engineering roadmap is driven by cost per covered user rather than by peak throughput.

charter.mission: We are a long-dated energy bet. Our job this decade is not revenue; it is to reach a grid-scale customer and a cost curve that someone outside the group is willing to finance.
charter.process: We run to a published cost model that Finance signs off on, and every experiment is scored by how much it moves the 2032 number rather than by whether it worked. External funding is pursued deliberately, because a bet only the group will fund is a bet nobody has checked.

charter.mission: We are the investor inside the group. We fund the bets, we gate them, and we are the ones who have to say the word when a bet has run out of road.
charter.process: Every bet passes a quarterly gate on two questions: who is the buyer, and is there a signed pilot. Bets that fail twice are wound down or sold. Every bet sits on the same board cadence with the same pack, so they can be compared rather than described.

charter.mission: We run the compute, storage, network and power the whole group sits on, and we intend it to cost less per unit of work every year even as the work grows faster than the budget.
charter.process: Capacity is planned three years out against the AI training and serving forecast, with a six-month rolling revision. Accelerator, data centre and network roadmaps are one plan; a weekly capacity review reads out committed power before it reads out anything else.
owns: cost per unit of served compute

charter.mission: We keep the group's surfaces safe enough that no regulator has to write the policy for us. We would rather take the hit for enforcing a rule than have one imposed on us.
charter.process: Policy is written by Content Policy, enforced by Enforcement Operations, and the two are deliberately separate so a policy cannot be quietly softened because it is hard to enforce. Severity-1 queues are staffed continuously; appeal overturn rates are published internally every month.

charter.mission: We make a breach of one product stop being a breach of the account. Our measure is not how many attacks we stopped but how little a successful one gets.
charter.process: Every production service sits behind the zero-trust proxy or has a dated exception signed by a director. Critical findings run to a seven-day SLA, not to the end of the quarter, and we run unannounced exercises against production rather than against a staging clone.

charter.mission: We turn regulatory pressure into specifications engineers can build against, early enough that the build is a roadmap item rather than an emergency.
charter.process: Competition matters are run to agreed remedies rather than to indefinite appeals, and within 30 days of an agreement the product team gets a written remedy spec. Public Policy files the group's position in every market writing rules that will bind us, whether or not we were invited.

charter.mission: We keep the people the operating plan quietly assumes are already here, and we move people into the roles the plan needs rather than only hiring them from outside.
charter.process: A rolling hiring plan runs against the operating plan with priority roles named by division. Internal mobility is treated as a hiring channel with its own funnel, and promotion rates are reconciled against the stated rates by level every half.
owns: the hiring plan and priority roles

charter.mission: We fund the second engine out of the first engine's efficiency rather than out of new money, and we give every division numbers it cannot argue with.
charter.process: One unit-economics model serves the whole group, so divisions argue about assumptions rather than about methodology. Capex is planned against operating cash flow with a hard line at the buyback, and the books close on a five-day clock.
owns: operating expense as a share of revenue

charter.mission: We make the group's second engine legible to the people who buy it. An enterprise buyer who cannot name our cloud is a deal Sales never gets invited to.
charter.process: Brand and Product Marketing plan one calendar against the pipeline Cloud Sales needs. Launch kits are measured by rep usage rather than by delivery, and campaign production is pulled in-house where the volume justifies it.
